comment: The native ctest job runs in a container on a GitHub hosted runner. These suites are excluded there because they fail on that runner specifically, not merely 'in a container' -- each passes in the same image on a real host, including under a 4-core cpuset with full ctest contention. This file exists so the exclusion set cannot grow silently: scripts/validate_native_ci_exclusions.py asserts the workflow's ctest -E expression names exactly these suites, so adding or removing one fails until it is declared with a reason. The declaration carries no authority over what runs; the workflow does.
covered_by: scripts/acceptance.sh on a real host, run by hand -- nothing schedules it

exclusions.reason: pins the session procfs with openat2, which the hosted sandbox does not permit
asserts inventory and occupancy digests built from a real host
spawns the live stack, which needs an authority directory whose whole ancestry is unwritable by others
builds a sealed worker artifact from the real runtime closure
